create.name: Magnolia Grove Monastery
create.bio:
Magnolia Grove is a monastery where nuns and monks live and train, and also a mindfulness practice centre of the Plum Village tradition near Batesville in northern Mississippi, one of three such monasteries in the United States alongside Deer Park and Blue Cliff. Thich Nhat Hanh founded it in 2005 on some 120 acres bought by a group of lay families, who built a large meditation hall, a kitchen and a guesthouse for visitors. Today nuns and monks, many of them Vietnamese, live there with lay residents.

Guests can join the community's daily rhythm on personal retreats starting on a Friday, attend themed retreats through the year such as a family week and a New Year retreat, or come on most Sundays for a public Day of Mindfulness supported by donations. The monastery also keeps a three-month rains retreat each winter. Its YouTube channel, active since 2011, carries the monastics' Dharma talks in English and Vietnamese from Sundays and retreats, along with short films about life at the monastery.

courses.title: Holiday Retreat 2026: The Art of Love
courses.description: The monastery's year-end retreat on love as a daily practice, with sitting, walking and eating meditation, Dharma talks and time with the monastic community.

courses.title: Personal retreats
courses.description: Stays of a weekend, a week or longer, arriving on a Friday, following the monastery's schedule of practice with monks, nuns and lay guests.

free_resources.title: Sunday Day of Mindfulness
free_resources.description: Most Sundays the monastery opens to the public for a day of meditation, a Dharma talk and mindful practice together; donations welcome.
